reports.title: Omeros Corporation Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

desk.headline: YARTEMLEA net sales up 26% q/q to $35.9m, slightly below estimates; $57.4m net loss on derivative charge; no guidance
results: Net sales of YARTEMLEA, its drug for a rare stem-cell-transplant complication, rose 26% from Q2 to $35.9m, a little under the $37.3m expected; there were no sales a year ago.
More sales went to discount-eligible 340B hospitals, lifting the gap between gross and net sales to 14.0% from 11.5%.
Operating profit was $4.5m and operating cash flow a positive $13.3m, the second positive quarter in a row.
A $62.0m non-cash charge, mainly on a derivative tied to its 2029 convertible notes, produced a GAAP loss of $57.4m ($0.79 a share); excluding it, adjusted profit was $4.7m.
Bought back $30.5m of 2029 notes for $60.2m in July; in October European regulators confirmed their negative opinion on the drug.

guidance.summary: Omeros gives no financial guidance. It said YARTEMLEA sales kept growing into Q4.

watch: YARTEMLEA growth in Q4 now that the extra Medicare inpatient payment (NTAP) applies from 1 October.
How far 340B sales keep pushing up the gross-to-net discount.
Near-term milestone payments from Novo on zaltenibart and start of new YARTEMLEA studies.
